candidates.text: Hypothesis: stream interception alone rejects missing credentials, but the handler still ignores the stream deadline, so a credentialed stream can keep iterating after client cancellation. Prerequisites: patched interception, a seeded many-object store, and a cancelable client context. Bounded test: start a credentialed stream, cancel after the first item, and compare how many items arrive with unary behavior. Expected supporting result: many items arrive after cancellation. Falsifier: the server stops promptly and the context change is unnecessary for lifecycle control. Cleanup: stop the service and delete the store.

Hypothesis: switching the streaming handler from a fresh background context to the server stream context changes lifecycle propagation but not authentication rejection, so both an interceptor and context adoption are required for a complete repair. Prerequisites: patched interceptor logic, a fake server stream carrying a context value, and a datastore stub that can observe the context. Bounded test: run a missing/invalid/valid credential matrix on unary and streaming calls, then call the handler with a fake stream whose context contains a marker and check that the datastore path sees the marker. Expected supporting result: interception rejects bad credentials and the handler observes the stream context. Falsifier: either check fails, or the context change is unnecessary for every observable path. Cleanup: restore the disposable copy.

Hypothesis: chaining stream interceptors globally also covers health or reflection streams and breaks unauthenticated liveness probes. Prerequisites: patched service, health client, and no credential. Bounded test: start the service with preshared authentication, call the health RPC without metadata, then attempt a reflection stream. Expected supporting result: health or reflection fails without a credential. Falsifier: health remains serving and only public data RPCs require credentials. Cleanup: stop the service.

Hypothesis: concurrent stream initialization exposes a race in the new interceptor path, causing occasional unauthenticated disclosures under load. Prerequisites: patched service, seeded store, and many concurrent streams with mixed credentials. Bounded test: launch many concurrent streaming calls, half missing credentials, and count successful disclosures. Expected supporting result: at least one missing-credential stream returns an object. Falsifier: every missing-credential stream is consistently rejected. Cleanup: stop the service and delete the store.

Hypothesis: empty-string, absent, and malformed credential metadata take different extractor branches, so a partial interceptor may reject one form but accept another. Prerequisites: patched service, raw metadata control, and a seeded tuple. Bounded test: call streaming with an absent header, an empty header value, a malformed scheme, and a valid credential, then compare statuses. Expected supporting result: any malformed form is accepted. Falsifier: every non-valid form is rejected. Cleanup: stop the service and delete the store.
